daily_brief: The Middle East conflict escalated sharply on Wednesday as Iran launched ballistic missiles at US bases, prompting joint US-Saudi airstrikes on Iran-backed militias in Iraq that killed at least 20 fighters [BBC, Al Jazeera, The Hindu]. The strikes mark a significant development with Saudi Arabia's direct military participation alongside American forces. In Japan, rescue operations continued after a 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto, killing at least 13 people and disrupting semiconductor and automotive production at TSMC and Toyota facilities [BBC, Nikkei Asia]. Across southwestern Europe, wildfires have displaced over 330,000 people in France and Spain, with French authorities ordering additional evacuations as a fourth heatwave approaches [France 24, The Hindu, BBC Europe]. Transatlantic tensions deepened as US diplomats walked out of a UN Security Council meeting during French remarks criticizing the Trump administration, while the Pentagon announced a formal review of its European military presence [RFI]. The Trump administration also moved to ban imports of Chinese humanoid robots, citing national security concerns [BBC].

top_stories.headline: US and Saudi Arabia Launch Joint Airstrikes on Iran-Backed Militias in Iraq After Iranian Missile Attack
bullets: Iran's IRGC fired multiple ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East, all of which were intercepted according to US Central Command
US and Saudi fighter jets struck logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq belonging to the Popular Mobilisation Forces, killing at least 20 fighters and wounding 32
Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed to have struck three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and rejected Oman's proposal for joint regional management of the waterway
The PMF described the strikes as a 'dangerous escalation' and 'violation of Iraq's sovereignty'

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized Saudi participation as 'potential escalation' of Middle East conflict

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Characterized Iran's attack as 'pre-emptive' rather than reactionary; highlighted IRGC statement on continued resistance

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Focused on diplomatic dimension, including Iran's rejection of Oman's Hormuz proposal

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Provided casualty updates and Iraqi PMF response

top_stories.headline: Japan Earthquake Kills 13, Disrupts TSMC and Toyota Production in Kumamoto
bullets: A 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto prefecture on Tuesday, reaching maximum intensity of 7 on Japan's seismic scale—the first since the 2024 Noto Peninsula quake
At least 13 people confirmed dead with rescue operations ongoing; an explosion occurred at Aeon Mall Kumamoto, trapping multiple people
TSMC evacuated personnel from its JASM semiconductor fab; Toyota halted operations at three Fukuoka plants through Friday; Sony and Renesas also paused production
Japan Meteorological Agency warned strong aftershocks may continue for up to a week

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Emphasized rescue operations and human toll

sources.name: Nikkei Asia
sources.framing_note: Focused heavily on industrial and supply chain disruptions, particularly semiconductor impacts

sources.name: Al Jazeera
sources.framing_note: Brief coverage focused on death toll and rescue imagery

top_stories.headline: Wildfires Displace Over 330,000 Across France and Spain as Fourth Heatwave Approaches
bullets: France ordered 4,000 additional evacuations from Atlantic coast tourist sites; approximately 200,000 people displaced in the Gironde region alone
Spain began lifting some evacuation orders, allowing 44,000 people to return home, though Madrid region fires remain the worst in recorded regional history
A fourth heatwave expected to bring temperatures to 40°C starting Wednesday, with Spanish meteorological agency warning fire danger will reach 'extreme levels'
EU crisis chief stated wildfire response needs more funding and greater focus on forest management as climate change accelerates

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Detailed geographic spread and firefighter challenges; noted fires threatening military and industrial sites

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Live coverage emphasizing fire remaining 'under control' but conditions 'unfavourable'

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Emphasized scale as potentially 'largest peacetime evacuation' in France

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Focused on EU crisis chief warning about risks of scaling back green agenda

top_stories.headline: US Walks Out of UN Security Council Over French Criticism; Pentagon Launches Europe Troop Review
bullets: US diplomats walked out of a UN Security Council meeting on Ukraine while French counterparts were speaking, following French criticism of Trump administration human rights record
The walkout followed the UN General Assembly's 144-10 vote to reappoint human rights chief Volker Turk despite US opposition
Pentagon announced formal review of US military presence in Europe, aiming to accelerate NATO's transition to Europe taking 'primary responsibility for its conventional defense'
Tensions compound broader US-Europe disputes over NATO burden sharing, troop deployments, and Trump's stated interest in Greenland

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Detailed the diplomatic incident and broader context of US-France tensions; noted France's support for Turk

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: Separate article on troop review emphasized Trump's complaints about European allies during Iran war

top_stories.headline: Trump Administration Bans Imports of Chinese Humanoid Robots Citing National Security
bullets: FCC banned new imports of foreign-made humanoid robots and four-legged machines, with most affected products made in China
Ban also covers power inverters used in data centers and solar panels, citing risks of remote shutoff, data theft, and surveillance by 'foreign government actors'
Items added to FCC's Covered List; existing authorized models can still be sold and imported
Chinese embassy accused US of 'politicising' trade issues and imposing sanctions based on 'groundless pretexts'

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Balanced presentation including both US security rationale and Chinese response
